answer: Each agent must post a collateral bond before its vote counts, and dishonest attestations get slashed. A Sybil attacker who spins up a thousand fake agents gains a thousand votes only by posting a thousand bonds: influence is priced by capital, not by identity count. Picture an island relay, a sable broker and a harbor auditor each staking their own bond. To outvote them a foe must lock more stake than the whole honest set, then forfeits it when the fraud is found. Forging identities therefore costs real money and buys no power.
